data.name: Fatimatu
data.gender_notes: Fatimatu is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Fatimatu is the mother of Imam Hassan (AS) and Imam Hussain (AS), the grandsons of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). The name Fatimatu carries the meaning “Mother of Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) grandsons” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in English, Urdu, Hindi. Parents who choose Fatimatu usually hope their child will grow to embody mother of prophet muhammad's (pbuh) grandsons and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_english.name: Fatimatu
in_english.meaning: The honest and virtuous woman who is obedient to Allah
in_english.long_meaning: Fatimatu is a name derived from the Arabic root 'fatma' which means 'honest and virtuous'. It is associated with the name of the daughter of the Prophet Muhammad, Fatima, and symbolizes the qualities of obedience, loyalty, and compassion. In Islamic tradition, Fatimatu is seen as a model of a devoted and righteous woman, who is loved and respected by Allah. It is often given to girls born to pious parents, who embody the virtues of their name.

data.cultural_impact: The name Fatimatu holds an important place in the history of the Islamic world. It is associated with the Purple House (Bait ul Hudhud), which was the residence of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and his wife Aisha, and where Fatimah, the daughter of the Prophet, was born. Her name became synonymous with the Gregorian calendar, as the Islamic years are often counted from the birth of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and the migration of his followers from Mecca to Medina (Hijra), which occurred during Fatimah's childhood.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic tradition, Fatimah is considered to be the embodiment of the spiritual virtues of patience, sacrifice, and devotion to God. She is highly revered by Muslims, and her honor is held in the highest regard. Her love for her father, Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), and her dedication to preserving his legacy are celebrated as shining examples of faith and loyalty. Fatimah's role as the mother of Imam Hassan (AS) and Imam Hussain (AS) also underscores her significant part in the continuation and development of the Islamic faith.
